patch.value: Branch-local and compound-line publish bindings let an unattested npm publish pass the attestation gate

The canonical auditor resolves shell scalars by numeric scope depth only, so a binding assigned in one branch of an if/else is visible in the mutually exclusive sibling branch, and its assignment matcher is anchored to the start of a line, so an assignment inside a one-line compound command is never recorded. Both make the gate attest a publish it has not proven: the first reports an unattested publish as carrying --provenance, the second hides the publish entirely and lets an attested sibling satisfy the non-vacuity guard.

A scalar bound only in a then-branch is not visible to a publish in the else-branch; the auditor refuses rather than attests; An assignment inside a one-line compound command is recorded, and the publish it routes is discovered; Each fix has a regression test verified to fail when the fix alone is reverted; No coverage or docstring regression; the gate stays at 100/100/100/100

value.text:
Reproduced both fail-open paths by executing auditPublishAttestation. Before the fix, the if/else workflow returned failures: [] with the ok note, and the two-job compound workflow returned recognition {kind:"recognized",count:1} with failures: [].

Red-on-revert proof:
1. Branch identity: removed only the sibling-arm clearing block in attestation.ts (`if (startsIfSiblingArm(segment) || (insideCase && startsCaseArm(segment))) scopes[scopes.length - 1]!.clear()`). The test "a binding from one conditional arm cannot attest a publish in its sibling arm" failed at its first assertion with actual 0 failures versus expected 1. Restored the block; the test passed.
2. Compound assignments: removed the compound-position token loop from literalScalarAssignments in shell-scan.ts and reverted the unresolved-program candidate fallback in attestation.ts to the former npm/foreign-publisher filter. The test "a compound-line assignment exposes the unattested publish it routes" failed with recognition count 1 versus expected 2. Restored both hunks; the test passed with recognition count 2 and one unattested-publish failure.

The reported heredoc construction was not changed; no executing fail-open reproduction exists for it.

patch.value: Canonical attestation expansion now tracks sibling branch identity, applies scope transitions per shell segment, records provable compound assignments, and fails closed on unresolved publisher variables.
Sibling-arm bindings cannot attest each other; one-line compound assignments expose routed publishes; uncertainty refuses.
Both reproduced bypasses now produce one failure; compound reproduction recognizes two publishes; branch, case, and uncertainty regressions pass.

Branch-local scalar evidence is cleared at if/elif/else and case-arm boundaries; compound-line literal assignments are tokenized and variable-routed publishes are discovered or refused. Both regressions are red-on-revert, all mandatory gates passed at 100% coverage.
